11/07/2020

Dr B White
Neurosurgeon
City Hospital
Newtown

Dear Dr White,
Re: Mr George Poulos, aged 45

I am writing to refer Mr Poulos, a 45-year-old stocker, who has a lower back pain suggestive of disc prolapsed associated with a radiculopathy. He requires your evaluation and management, possibility (possibly) including surgery.

Mr Poulos smokes 25 cigarettes and drinks 10-15 unite (units) of alcohol per day. He is allergic to penicillin, pethidine and radiographic contrast agent.

Initially, on 21/06/2014, Mr Poulos presented to me complaining (complained “more concise”) of sudden lower back pain which had occurred two days previously while he was (during) lifting a heavy object. It had been associated with a click sensation without any radiation, and it had improved with analgesia. His musculo-skeletal examination revealed loss of lumbar lordosis and limitation of flexion and extension movements. Therefore, he was advised to rest and he was commenced on paracetamol, 1 gr every four hours, alternating with Panadeine Forte. 

Over the past two weeks, Mr Poulos` condition has worsened with a radiation to his right leg and movement limitation due the pain. His examination today showed (an) almost a stiff lower back associated with loss of light touch sensation on the lateral distal calf and planter aspect of (the) foot. In addition to (, there was / he had) limitation of (the) straight left leg raise to 70 and left (right) leg to 50, along with, loss of (the) right ankle refluxe (reflex).
Given these finding, I am referring Mr Poulos for further investigation, possibly including an MRI, and for your advice on (the) possibility of surgery. 
For any quires, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
